clue.text: Involving many parties, like 23

definitions.meaning: describes an agreement or talks with several sides taking part
entry 23 is an eight-sided figure, so it has many sides

explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means many-sided: diplomatically that is several nations taking part, geometrically a shape with numerous edges.

clue.text: Wife Lot observed becoming salt

parts.note: a wife is a mate, a spouse
taken as written: the Biblical Lot

explanation.surface: Lot looks on as his wife turns into a pillar of salt, as in Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' seems to recall the pillar of salt Lot's wife became, but here it means an old sailor; 'observed becoming' is just linking.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is a seasoned sailor, and a French-derived slang word for a sailor is this one.

clue.text: Make generous allowance for big vessel

parts.note: big means large
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone makes a generous allowance in order to buy a big ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is a liberal gift or bounty bestowed freely, a generous handout.

clue.text: Change in dialect without distinction

indicators.note: to change the given words is to rearrange their letters into something new

explanation.surface: A shift in a regional dialect leaves speech without any distinctive features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges the nine letters of IN DIALECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are exactly alike have no distinguishing difference between them.

clue.text: In place of English races, one from another country

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
a Scot comes from Scotland, a country other than England

explanation.surface: At an English race meeting, one visitor comes from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, home of Royal Ascot; 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse is famous for its royal summer meeting of horse racing.

clue.text: Growth of Mediterranean seaport being rebuilt

indicators.note: a port being rebuilt has its parts put together in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean seaport is growing as it is reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rebuilt' rearranges the letters of SEAPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass growing in Spain and North Africa, used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Theologian, in a way, following Biblical character

indicators.note: the words 'a way' come after the Biblical character, so they are placed behind it

parts.note: Abel, son of Adam and Eve, slain by Cain
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A theologian follows the example of a Biblical figure, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' reads as 'after a fashion', but 'a way' gives A RD; Peter Abelard was a twelfth-century French theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a medieval French scholastic philosopher and teacher of divinity, famed also for Heloise.

clue.text: Master a Liberal — gain this, possibly

definitions.text: Master a Liberal — gain this, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the given letters may be arranged in some other order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, a British political party

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: beat a Liberal and win the constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MASTER, A, L and GAIN; the whole clue also describes the answer, since a narrowly held constituency is what beating a Liberal might win.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency held by a small majority is one that a rival party could take at an election.

clue.text: One goddess about to play leading role as another

indicators.note: the goddess's name goes about, that is around, the word for taking the lead part

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
to star is to take the leading role in a play or film

explanation.surface: One goddess is about to take the lead part, playing another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container and 'to' belongs with 'play leading role'; Astarte is a Phoenician goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of love and fertility, so she is a further deity beside Ate.

clue.text: Change of personnel in force

definitions.meaning: loose coins of low value, pennies and the like
members of the police force, slang for police officers

explanation.definitionFit: Small bronze coins are colloquially called this, and so are police officers, in British slang.

clue.text: Horst cheated?

parts.note: this word is a set of letters which, rearranged, spell the word short, so it is short in a changed form

explanation.walkthrough: Horst is the word SHORT with its letters changed around, so the clue is wordplay read backwards from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swindled by being given too little money back in a purchase is to be diddled.

clue.text: Navigator involved with Cornish pirates?

definitions.meaning: Sir Humphrey, the Elizabethan explorer who claimed Newfoundland
W. S. of the comic opera partnership that wrote The Pirates of Penzance, set in Cornwall

explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance is a comic opera; Penzance is a town in Cornwall, the county at England's far south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to an Elizabethan seafaring explorer and to the librettist of the Savoy operas.

clue.text: Fuss about navy, with onset of Atlantic storm

indicators.note: the word for a fuss goes about, around, the navy and the first letter that follow

parts.note: a to-do is a commotion or fuss
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so just its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Panic about the fleet as an Atlantic storm begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal and 'onset of' takes just the opening letter of Atlantic; a to-do is British for a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, a kind of tempest.

clue.text: Observes make-up of badge, for instance

definitions.meaning: remarks on or takes heed of something
the word badge is spelt entirely with the musical letters B, A, D, G and E

explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to make a mention of something, and the letters A to G name musical pitches, from which the word badge is built.

clue.text: Agreement on string to use in whip

indicators.note: the words before are to be put to use inside the whip, so they go within it

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
taken as written
cord is string

explanation.surface: Two parties agree on which string to use in making a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use in' is the container signal; the cat-o'-nine-tails was a naval flogging whip, and a concordat is chiefly a pact between the Vatican and a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal pact, particularly one between the Pope and a government.

clue.text: Churchwarden barred by this commandment?

parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, so the rule forbidding it is a ban on lighting up, not a church edict

explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe as well as a parish officer; the 'commandment' is a sign forbidding tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice banning tobacco would prohibit puffing on a long clay pipe.

clue.text: Means of evading law used in defence

definitions.meaning: gaps or ambiguities in legislation that let someone escape its intent
narrow slits in castle walls for archers to shoot through

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ambiguity exploited to dodge a rule and an arrow slit in a fortification.

clue.text: Make mistake in Times? Continue to next page

definitions.meaning: to run past the allotted time, exceeding a deadline
in printing, text carried over beyond the end of a page or column

explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' teasingly names the newspaper, but here it means durations, which can be exceeded.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means going beyond a time limit, and in typesetting, text spilling over beyond a column or page.

clue.text: In awkward situation, it's upsetting to be unfriendly

indicators.note: the opening word puts the next piece in, that is inside, the awkward situation

parts.note: being in a hole means being in an awkward fix

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word up, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Being in a tight spot is upsetting enough to make anyone surly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start is the container signal, and 'upsetting' turns 'it's' backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostile manner is antagonistic, the opposite of amicable.

clue.text: Run ashore, say — get mast from one

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, so a word of like sound is entered

parts.note: to beach a boat is to run it up on the shore

explanation.surface: A sailor beaches the boat and fetches a new mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mast' seems nautical, but beech mast is the nuts that fall from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the fallen nuts of forest trees, and this tree drops large quantities of it.

clue.text: Like leader of Druids in relation to C.E.

definitions.text: Like leader of Druids in relation to C.E.

parts.words: Like leader of Druids in relation to C.E.
parts.note: the first letter of Druids is D, which in the alphabet sits flanked by the letters C and E

explanation.walkthrough: 'C.E.' looks like Common Era or Church of England, but is just the letters C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: D sits in the middle of C and E in the alphabet, flanked on each side.

clue.text: Make a deep impression in French accent

parts.note: the French for in is en
the grave is an accent sloping down to the right, as in à

explanation.surface: A French accent leaves a strong mark on listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave is literally to cut deeply into a surface, and figuratively to fix firmly in the mind.

clue.text: Engineers brought back sound for French American writer

indicators.note: brought back means the abbreviation is turned round and read in the reverse direction

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
son is the French word for sound

explanation.surface: Army engineers returned with French audio equipment for a US author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns REME into EMER; 'French American' reads as one phrase, but 'French' goes with 'sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century New England essayist and poet.

clue.text: Doyle's knight gets support in rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the pieces are read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A knight in a Conan Doyle tale is helped back to his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses LEG IN as a whole; Sir Nigel is the hero of Arthur Conan Doyle's historical novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Nigel Loring is the chivalrous hero of Conan Doyle's novel Sir Nigel and The White Company.

clue.text: Go on and act parts for a certain figure

indicators.note: parts suggests the given words are broken up and their pieces put together afresh

explanation.surface: Actors carry on and play their parts for a particular person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges GO ON and ACT; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a specific geometric shape, a polygon with eight sides.

clue.text: Forming a revolutionary movement

definitions.meaning: shaping wood or metal on a lathe

explanation.definitionFit: On a lathe, shaping a piece is done as it rotates, and the word also means simply spinning round.

clue.text: Repeat start with same letter, after all

indicators.note: the answer comes after the word all in the longer word, so all is removed from its front

parts.note: to alliterate is to begin neighbouring words with one sound
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to repeat the opening letter, after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after all' looks like 'nevertheless', but the answer is the part of the longer word that follows the three letters of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, to reiterate.

clue.text: One has no reason to want such news

definitions.text: One has no reason to want such news

parts.words: One has no reason to want such news
parts.note: news here means secret information, and someone lacking reason is short of brains, the same word covering both

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both mental capacity and gathered information, so the witless person lacks it and spies want it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both mental ability and secret military or political information.
